title: 2005 AMC 10A Problem 25
statement: In \(\triangle ABC\) we have \(AB = 25,\) \(BC = 39,\) and \(AC = 42.\) Points \(D\) and \(E\) are on \(AB\) and \(AC\) respectively, with \(AD = 19\) and \(AE = 14.\) What is the ratio of the area of triangle \(ADE\) to the area of the quadrilateral \(BCED?\)

solutions.text:
Triangles \(ADE\) and \(ABC\) share angle \(A,\) so \[ \begin{aligned} \dfrac{[ADE]}{[ABC]} &= \dfrac{AD \cdot AE}{AB \cdot AC} \\ &= \dfrac{19 \cdot 14}{25 \cdot 42} \\ &= \dfrac{266}{1050} \\ &= \dfrac{19}{75}. \end{aligned} \] Since \([BCED] = [ABC] - [ADE],\) we get \(\dfrac{[ADE]}{[BCED]} = \dfrac{19}{75 - 19} = \dfrac{19}{56}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Triangles sharing angle \(A\) satisfy \(\dfrac{[ADE]}{[ABC]} = \dfrac{AD \cdot AE}{AB \cdot AC}\)
The quadrilateral is the remaining part: \([BCED] = [ABC] - [ADE]\)
